---
title: What an app sees
description: What a Calimero app instance sees once it runs on a cluster — init arguments, callers, organizations and teams, events, blobs, upgrades, outbound requests, confirmations and limits.
---

An **app instance** is one running copy of your package: its own state, its owner, an access rule, and its own Raft
log on (by default) three nodes. This page covers what your code sees inside one. The complete list is in the core
reference's [Writing apps for a cluster](https://calimero-network.github.io/core/cloud/apps/).

## Creation and init

An instance is created from a package release, with **init arguments** (JSON) that your `#[app::init]` receives.
`init` runs once, on the instance's first leader, as the instance's owner. If it fails, the instance is not left
half-made: creation answers `422 INIT_FAILED` with your error.

Each organization that uses your app gets its own instance, so init arguments are per organization. See
[Deploy & instances](/cloud/deploy/).

## Who is calling

- **The caller.** `env::account_id()` is the signed-in account. A person's devices are passkeys on one account, so
  there is one id per person, whichever device they use.
- **The organization.** `env::caller_org()` returns the caller's standing in the instance's organization (its id,
  their role and the teams they are in), or `None`. The node already keeps non-members out; use this for rules
  inside the app:

  ```rust
  use calimero_sdk::env::{self, OrgRole};

  pub fn set_pinned(&mut self, text: String) -> app::Result<()> {
      if !env::caller_org().is_some_and(|o| o.role >= OrgRole::Admin) {
          app::bail!("admins only");
      }
      self.pinned.set(text);
      Ok(())
  }
  ```

- **The instance.** `env::context_id()` is the instance's id as the app sees it.

## Calls, views and ordering

Calls to one instance apply in one order on its leader, so a write never races another write. Views read state
without changing it. Strong reads go through the leader; a client may ask for a faster read from any replica. A
caller that cannot reach the cluster cannot write, so there are no offline edits to reconcile later.

## Events

`app::emit!` publishes an event with the call that emitted it. Clients stream an instance's events
(`client.events(app)` in mero-js, `meroctl context watch`). Methods marked `#[app::handler]` can run in response to an
event, once, on the leader.

## Blobs and search

`env::blob_*` store and open content-addressed bytes that belong to the instance; clients upload and download them
through the same sealed channel. `#[derive(app::Searchable)]` declares full-text indexes that views can query.

## Cross-app calls and timers

An `#[app::xcall]` method can be called by other apps in the same organization. `#[app::tee(every = "..")]` methods run
on a schedule.

## Outbound HTTPS

A call may send an HTTPS request under a URL prefix your signed manifest declares, once that prefix is approved for
your package by whoever the cluster's rules give that decision (the instance's owner, or the operator). Until then
the request is refused with `NotApproved`, which your app can show.

## Confirmations

Methods listed in an instance's `confirmMethods` need a fresh passkey assertion over the exact call
(`callConfirmed` in the clients). Use it for anything a person must explicitly agree to, such as a payment or a
deletion.

## Upgrades

A new version upgrades an instance in place. Mark your state's version with `#[app::state(version = ..)]` and write
an `#[app::migrate]` function; the cluster plans the migration from the two versions' embedded ABIs and refuses a
downgrade or a missing migration. Who may upgrade is decided per cluster: the instance's owner (with a passkey
step-up) or the operator.

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Package size | 16 MiB |
| One call's log entry (arguments, state change and events) | 1 MiB |
| Instances, package bytes, API keys and organizations per account | Quotas set by the operator (`429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED`) |
